subject: Structured output degradation — request for temporary SLA exemption and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenLeaf SRE <sre@greenleafhealth.com>, contracts@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Hi Sergio / Laura,

We started seeing a spike in structured-output validation failures and tool-call timeouts this morning across three tenant regions. The downstream effect is that our patient-summary generation pipeline is timing out and retrying, which trips our side of the SLA monitoring. We collected a set of sample errors and attached one log excerpt (prod-error-sample-20270912.log).

Can Redwood consider a temporary carve-out/exemption in the SLA for incidents attributable to structured-output toolchain degradation while we work through the mitigation? GreenLeaf needs a documented commitment window and a remediation plan so we can explain to our compliance team.

Requested: 1) Temporary exclusion window for latency penalties tied specifically to 'structured output -> tool call' failures (we anticipate 48-72 hours), 2) A technical mitigation plan and ETA, and 3) A named engineering contact for real-time troubleshooting.

Thanks,
Asha
Director, Platform Operations
GreenLeaf Health
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Hi Asha — thank you for the detailed report and the logs. Sorry you're seeing this in prod. I pulled Neha and Aditya into the thread; they own the runtime and model-tooling respectively.

Quick summary of immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Neha will triage logs and identify whether this is kernel/quantization fallout or an upstream model change.
- Aditya will validate if recent structured-output validation heuristics have regressed under long context lengths.
- We'll stand up an extended troubleshooting channel and provide hourly updates.

On the SLA carve-out: we can propose a short-term, documented exemption that excludes 'structured-output + external toolcall timeout' events from availability calculations for a limited window, provided GreenLeaf accepts the mitigation plan and the temporary scope. We're targeting a proposed exemption window of 72 hours from the time we announce the mitigation rollout.

I'll schedule a call in the next 30 minutes with SRE if that's amenable.

— Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Stack findings so far (initial triage):
- Error signature indicates repeated 504-style toolcall timeouts originating from the external webhook adapter when structured-output candidates included nested JSON arrays larger than ~12k chars.
- Runtime telemetry shows elevated KV cache misses during long-sequence requests coincident with the failures.
- No infra scaling events at the time; appears to be an algorithmic regression in the structured-output postprocessor sending oversized payloads to the tool invocation layer.

Immediate remediation plan (0–24h):
1) Roll a hotfix to cap structured-output candidate payloads to 8k chars and stream long candidates (hotfix v1).
2) Enable a fallback route that returns a compact, non-structured summary when toolcall failure rate exceeds threshold (toggle via config).
3) Add extra logging and a temporary metric to track 'toolcall_payload_size' and 'structured_output_fallback_rate'.

If we get GreenLeaf signoff for the SLA carve-out, we will proceed with the hotfix and the fallback toggle. Otherwise we'll need to run the fallback immediately which may affect output formatting expectations.

Neha
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Asha — quick technical note on risk and rollback:
- The hotfix (payload cap + streaming) can be rolled to GreenLeaf's dedicated pool only (no cross-tenant risk) within ~3 hours of approval. We'll run it as a canary against 5% of traffic for 30 minutes and validate toolcall success rate and end-to-end latency.
- Fallback to compact summaries will preserve content but change the JSON schema; we will provide a compatibility header so your downstream parsers can detect and gracefully accept the alternate format.

If GreenLeaf wants a formal exemption window, propose we document the timeframe starting at the canary rollout time; Redwood will commit to the remediation activities and post-mortem.

Aditya
Lead, Tooling & Model Integrations
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Asha — thanks for patience; attached is a short mitigation plan and the proposed carve-out language we would add to the operational SLA while we remediate. Key points:
- Scope: Exemption applies only to availability/latency penalties when failures are demonstrably caused by structured-output -> toolcall payload/validation failures originating from Redwood's post-processing.
- Duration: 72-hour window starting at the canary rollout (we'll notify when we start).
- Commitments: Hourly updates during the window, a root cause analysis within 5 business days, and a one-time SLA credit if the root cause extends beyond the 72-hour window.

Please confirm acceptance of the scope and duration and we'll proceed with scheduling the canary tonight.

Laura
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenLeaf SRE <sre@greenleafhealth.com>, contracts@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Sep 2027 23:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden increase in structured-output errors / latency impacting care workflows

Laura / Sergio — GreenLeaf accepts the proposed scope and 72-hour exemption window starting at canary start. We also need the compatibility header documented and a short note for our compliance team that the exemption applies only to latency/availability calculations (not to data retention or security obligations).

Please share the canary start time and the primary on-call contact. If possible, include a brief customer-facing note we can send to our internal stakeholders explaining the temporary format fallback.

Thanks — Asha
Director, Platform Operations
GreenLeaf Health
